Method of Attack: Fake employment website distributing malware disguised as a desktop application for U.S. veterans
Malware downloads two additional malware files upon execution
One malware gathers extensive system and user information via 111 commands
Information is collected into a file and exfiltrated via embedded Gmail credentials
Second malware is a Remote Access Trojan (RAT) installed as a Windows service named 'dllhost' with display name 'Dll host'
RAT connects to attacker command & control servers to receive and execute commands, allowing full control over the victim's computer
Indicators of Compromise: Windows service display name: Dll host
Embedded Gmail email credentials used for data exfiltration
Attack Vector: Fake job opportunity website impersonating Hire Military Heroes (HMH) prompting users to download malware
